messages.content: "John has $5000 that he wants to invest. He is considering two options. The first option is a savings account that compounds interest quarterly at an annual rate of 4% for 5 years. The second option is a bond that offers simple interest at an annual rate of 3.5% for 5 years. How much would John have at the end of 5 years for both options?"

message.content:
**Option 1 – Quarterly‑compounded savings account**

| Parameter | Value |
|-----------|-------|
| Principal \(P\) | \$5 000 |
| Annual rate \(r\) | 4 % → 0.04 |
| Time \(t\) | 5 years |
| Compounding periods per year \(n\) | 4 |

The future value after \(t\) years with compounding \(n\) times per year is  

\[
A = P \left(1+\frac{r}{n}\right)^{nt}
\]

Plugging in the numbers:

\[
A = 5\,000 \left(1+\frac{0.04}{4}\right)^{4\times5}
   = 5\,000 \left(1+0.01\right)^{20}
   = 5\,000 \times 1.01^{20}
\]

\(1.01^{20}\approx 1.22019\)

\[
A \approx 5\,000 \times 1.22019 \approx \$6\,100.95
\]

So John would have **about \$6 101** after 5 years with the savings account.

---

**Option 2 – Simple‑interest bond**

| Parameter | Value |
|-----------|-------|
| Principal \(P\) | \$5 000 |
| Annual rate \(r\) | 3.5 % → 0.035 |
| Time \(t\) | 5 years |

With simple interest the future value is

\[
A = P \bigl(1 + rt\bigr)
\]

\[
A = 5\,000 \bigl(1 + 0.035 \times 5\bigr)
   = 5\,000 \bigl(1 + 0.175\bigr)
   = 5\,000 \times 1.175
   = \$5\,875
\]

So John would have **\$5 875** after 5 years with the bond.

---

### Summary

| Investment | Future value after 5 years |
|------------|---------------------------|
| Quarterly‑compounded savings account | **≈ \$6 101** |
| Simple‑interest bond | **\$5 875** |

The savings account yields roughly \$226 more than the bond over the five‑year period.
